question: What do we know about the generational wealth transfer, and how are these five preparing for it?

cells.label: different_quantity

items.text: The firm increased the cash component of advisor compensation in 2026 and reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors, changes described as supporting investment into financial advisors and simplifying the compensation program.
items.quote: we will also increase the cash component of our advisor compensation. We are making these changes to reduce the accounting-driven volatility in revenues and earnings. ... these changes support our overall investment into our financial advisors and will help simplify our compensation program.

items.text: In the first quarter of 2026 the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.
items.quote: in the first quarter of 2026, the Firm reduced the amount of deferred compensation as a proportion of total compensation for Wealth Management advisors.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027 and is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 advisor pay plan, adhering to a more traditional approach, unlike competitors.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Morgan Stanley uses deferred compensation as a retention tool, taking a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation and requiring advisors to stay for years to vest -- described as 'golden handcuffs.'
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest. If a financial advisor leaves a firm with a deferred compensation plan, he or she forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

cells.differs_because: The sub-question asks about how firms prepare for advisor succession and retirement given an aging advisor force and clients. The passages describe advisor compensation/retention mechanisms (deferred compensation, pay thresholds, cash compensation changes) rather than a succession or retirement-planning program for advisors or an aging advisor force figure.
cells.reason: No passage states a specific advisor succession/retirement preparation program or aging-advisor-force data; only related advisor compensation and retention measures are discussed.
